title: Developing Multi-Modal Operational Definitions
description: Construct behavioral, physiological, and self-report operational definitions for the complex psychological construct of 'empathy'.
problemStatement:
A developmental psychology lab wants to investigate whether reading fiction increases **empathy** in children aged 9 to 12. Empathy is an abstract, unobservable internal construct.

### Your Mission:
1. **Self-Report Operationalization**: Draft a 3-item self-report scale (using a 1-to-5 Likert format) suitable for measuring cognitive or emotional empathy in this age group.
2. **Behavioral Operationalization**: Design an observable behavioral scenario (e.g., an staged interaction in the waiting room or a resource-sharing game) that objectively quantifies empathic action.
3. **Physiological Operationalization**: Propose a non-invasive physiological indicator (e.g., facial electromyography of the zygomatic/corrugator muscles, pupillometry, or heart rate variability) that could index affective resonance.
4. **Triangulation Evaluation**: Briefly explain how synthesizing these three divergent data sources provides stronger construct validity than relying on any single measurement.
hints: Hint 1: For behavioral measures, consider counting measurable actions (e.g., helping pick up dropped crayons, donating game tokens).
Hint 2: For self-report, make items simple and age-appropriate (e.g., 'When my friend is crying, I feel sad too').
